primary_claim: Across 16 fresh NEON small-mammal sites, community-level multiscale spatial continuity was inherited from individual species rather than generated by turnover among species.
confirmatory_supported: 16/16 sites had maximum single-species continuity fraction 1.0.
0/16 sites had positive emergent connectivity gain.
0/16 sites had positive null-adjusted gain under the frozen assemblage-relocation null.
0/16 sites had a strict emergent world.
The one-sided aggregate sign-test p-value was 1.0.
exploratory_supported: Species richness was positively associated with the number of individually fully continuous species (rho 0.668; p 0.0047).
Species richness was negatively associated with dominance coverage (rho -0.594; p 0.015).
Species richness was not positively associated with cross-species rescue (rho -0.390; p 0.135).
prohibited: Species turnover never matters for community spatial structure.
The best continuity species is necessarily the dominant species.
The continuity assay directly measures dispersal or demographic connectivity.
ORNL proves that biodiversity generally decreases connectivity.
